items.title: Mandel Johnny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: The interviewee explains the origin of the title 'Groover Wailin'' referring to Grover Whalen, a historical figure, but does not mention any personal interaction with a person named 'Groover'.

ctx.x: Well, then I’m sure I did ‘cause I adore the way Gene Puerling writes. I was fortunate enough to work with him again on the – well not again but I mean work with him for the first time really on the Manhattan Transfer album we both wrote choral arrangements for that. In fact we split tunes, I’d write part of it, he’d write part, that sort of thing.

Just trying to put – just wrote it for instrumental. It was a play upon the guy who used to in the 30s, for some reason don't ask me why, I had some strange titles in my time, this guy was Grover Whalen and he was the official receptionist for New York. He used to lead all the tickertape parades for all the heroes that came in and he was sort of like the, he was the big guy all through the 20s, 30s and even 40s. He was a well known name and people around who heard that title would have known who I was talking…
